question_record.context: A security incident occurred where an attempt to disable the Microsoft Defender Antivirus service was detected, indicating a possible evasion attempt. Alongside this, malware detection indicated potential infection.
question_record.question: Following the tampering attempt with Microsoft Defender Antivirus, malware was detected. Can you find the name of the malware file that was identified?
solution: An attempt to disable the Microsoft Defender Antivirus service was detected on the host `vnevado-win10v`.
'Kekeo' malware was detected, specifically associated with the file `rubeus.exe`.

35.name: Microsoft Defender Antivirus tampering
35.description:
An attempt to disable the Microsoft Defender Antivirus service was detected. This might an attempt to evade detection.

For more information, read the Antivirus tampering technique profile Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/9ce0ac71-e104-4e59-9d46-2a8e2cac5a1d/analystreport.

92.name: 'Kekeo' malware was detected
92.description:
Malware and unwanted software are undesirable applications that perform annoying, disruptive, or harmful actions on affected machines. Some of these undesirable applications can replicate and spread from one machine to another. Others are able to receive commands from remote attackers and perform activities associated with cyber attacks.

This detection might indicate that the malware was stopped from delivering its payload. However, it is prudent to check the machine for signs of infection.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning
